cards.front: Who does DMV vision-test, and why?
cards.back: DMV vision-tests every applicant to confirm sight adequate for safe driving.

cards.front: What happens to your license if you take the vision test wearing glasses or contacts?
cards.back: Testing while wearing corrective or contact lenses puts a corrective lenses restriction on the license.

cards.front: Where does a failed vision test send you, and for what form?
cards.back: A failed vision test sends you to an eye doctor for a completed Report of Vision Examination (DL sixty-two) form.
cards.memory_hook: fail it, see the eye doctor

cards.front: Where are the vision standards detailed?
cards.back: Vision standards detail lives at dmv.ca.gov slash vision-standards.

cards.front: What kind of knowledge test does an original license require?
cards.back: An original license requires passing a knowledge test built from multiple choice questions.

cards.front: How many attempts do you get at the knowledge test before you must reapply?
cards.back: You get three attempts to pass before you must reapply.

cards.front: How long must a minor wait to retake a failed knowledge test?
cards.back: Minors wait seven days, excluding the failure day, before retaking a failed knowledge test.

cards.front: What may renewing drivers take instead of the knowledge test, and how does it work?
cards.back: Renewals may substitute eLearning, a no-fail self-paced interactive modulated course with quizzes after each module, taken on computer, laptop, tablet, or mobile device.

cards.front: When do testing options open up?
cards.back: Testing options open up once the application at dmv.ca.gov slash dl is complete.

cards.front: Which testing aids may you use during a knowledge test?
cards.back: No testing aids are allowed during knowledge tests, neither the handbook nor a cell phone.

cards.front: What are the format, attempts and minor retake wait of the knowledge test?
cards.back: The knowledge test bundles format, attempts, and retakes: multiple choice questions, three tries before reapplying, and a seven-day minor wait excluding the failure day.

cards.front: Who may use eLearning, and what can it never replace?
cards.back: eLearning is the renewal-only no-fail self-paced course with quizzes per module, never a substitute for the original-license knowledge test.

cards.front: Who must take a behind-the-wheel test?
cards.back: Original applicants take a behind-the-wheel test of safe driving ability, and renewing drivers with a vision or medical condition may have to take one too.

cards.front: Why might the examiner give two or more instructions at once?
cards.back: The examiner may stack two or more instructions at once to see whether you grasp and follow both.

cards.front: Where do you book a drive test appointment?
cards.back: Drive-test appointments are booked at dmv.ca.gov slash make-an-appointment.

cards.front: How long must a minor wait to retake a failed behind-the-wheel test?
cards.back: Minors wait fourteen days, excluding the failure day, before retaking a failed behind-the-wheel test.

cards.front: What does each of the three tests check?
cards.back: Three tests gate three things: vision screens eyesight, knowledge probes rules, and the drive test grades real skill.

decks.module: What to bring on test day

cards.front: Which document of your own should you bring on test day?
cards.back: On test day bring the instruction permit or license if one exists.

cards.front: Who must come with you on test day if you are not already licensed?
cards.back: Also bring another California-licensed driver aged at least eighteen, twenty-five for minors, unless already licensed to drive.

cards.front: What must the test vehicle and its papers include?
cards.back: Bring a vehicle safe for the test plus valid insurance proof and vehicle registration.

cards.front: When may a rental car be used for the drive test?
cards.back: Rental cars qualify only with your name on the rental contract and no contract clause excluding drive tests.

cards.front: What four categories must you bring on test day?
cards.back: Test day needs four bring-categories: papers for you, a licensed adult beside you, a legal car beneath you, and rental terms that permit testing.

cards.front: What does the pre-drive check start with?
cards.back: The pre-drive check starts with an opening driver window and a windshield giving you and the examiner a full, clear, unblocked view, since cracks can postpone the test.

cards.front: How many rearview mirrors must the test vehicle have, and where?
cards.back: At least two rearview mirrors are required, with one on the vehicle's left side.

cards.front: Which brake lights must work on the test vehicle?
cards.back: Both right and left brake lights must work.

cards.front: What tread depth must the tires have, and which spare is barred?
cards.back: Tires need at least one thirty-second-inch of uniformed tread depth, and donut tires are barred from the test.

cards.front: How much clearance must the pressed foot brake keep above the floorboard?
cards.back: The depressed foot brake must keep at least one inch of clearance above the floorboard.

cards.front: What must be true of the test vehicle's horn?
cards.back: The horn must be vehicle-designed, working, and audible from at least two hundred feet away.

cards.front: Which numbers must the test vehicle meet?
cards.back: The car's numbers cluster: at least two mirrors with one left, thirty-second-inch tread minimum, one inch of pedal clearance, and a horn heard at two hundred feet.

cards.front: What must you show about the parking brake?
cards.back: You must show how to set and release the parking brake.

cards.front: Which arm signals must you demonstrate?
cards.back: You must demonstrate the left turn, right turn, and slowing-or-stopping arm signals.

cards.front: What happens with the wipers and seat belts during the check?
cards.back: Wipers may be function-checked, and every seat belt must work and be worn by each occupant.

cards.front: What three demonstrations does the vehicle check ask for?
cards.back: The demo trio is hands, arms, and gear: set and release the parking brake, flash all three arm signals, and prove wipers plus belts.

cards.front: What happens if the vehicle fails the requirements?
cards.back: A vehicle that fails these requirements gets the drive test rescheduled.

cards.front: How far may an interpreter help during the drive test?
cards.back: Interpreters may help identify and use controls in the pre-drive inspection but cannot ride along for the test.

cards.front: Who may ride along on the drive test?
cards.back: Only the examiner accompanies the drive test, except for training, service animals, and certain law enforcement situations.

cards.front: What is the rule on recording devices during the drive test?
cards.back: Recording devices, including video recorders, are prohibited on the drive test, and one that cannot power off must be blocked from all visual and audio recording.

cards.front: What are the limits on riders, interpreters and recorders during the drive test?
cards.back: Only the examiner rides along, interpreters stop at the pre-drive inspection, and every recorder stays off or blocked.

cards.front: Which kind of vehicle technology is banned on the drive test, and why?
cards.back: Because the test grades the driver rather than the car, assistance tech such as automated parallel parking, lane departure, and adaptive cruise control is banned.

cards.front: Which vehicle safety technology is allowed, and what must you still do?
cards.back: Safety tech such as backup cameras and blind spot monitors is allowed yet never replaces direct mirror and blind-spot checks.

cards.front: How does banned assistance technology differ from allowed safety technology?
cards.back: Assistance tech that drives for you is banned, while safety tech that only shows you more is allowed yet never replaces your own eyes.

cards.front: Where can you find sample Driving Performance Evaluation Score Sheets?
cards.back: Sample Driving Performance Evaluation Score Sheets live at dmv.ca.gov slash teendriver, with Supplemental and Area sheets at dmv.ca.gov slash seniors.

recap_hooks.text: Every applicant is vision-tested; lenses add a restriction, and a failed test sends you to an eye doctor for the vision report form.
The original-license knowledge test is multiple choice, with three attempts before reapplying and a seven-day wait for minors after a failure.
Renewals may use eLearning instead, and no handbook or phone is allowed during a knowledge test.
Original applicants take a behind-the-wheel test, where the examiner may stack instructions, and minors wait fourteen days to retake a failed drive test.

recaps.module: What to bring on test day

recap_hooks.text: On test day bring your permit or license, a licensed companion if needed, and a safe insured registered vehicle; a rental needs your name and no drive test exclusion.
The test vehicle needs a clear windshield, two mirrors with one on the left, both brake lights, enough tread, pedal clearance of one inch and a working horn.
You show the parking brake, the three arm signals, the wipers and the belts, or the test is rescheduled.
Only the examiner rides along, interpreters stop at the pre-drive check, and recorders stay off or blocked.
Assistance technology is banned, while safety technology is allowed but never replaces your own checks.
